summary: The video side is one flat VHDL architecture built as a scan-time pipeline driven by 9-bit H/V raster counters. Tile RAM is time-shared with the CPU on H-counter phases, sprite RAM is scanned by counter bits into a pair of line buffers that are cleared after they are read, and PROM lookups are wired straight to the DAC bits. None of it follows MAME's tilemap/draw_sprites/screen_update split. The one clearly MAME-shaped part is the background scroll: a single scroll value from scrollram[0x40] for lines 64-127, a signed 16-bit per-line value made from the lo and hi scroll RAMs, and a clamp on overflow, which is the same rule as MAME's bitmap post-pass in draw_background. The sound board wires the AY bus-control pins and the MSM5205 control lines directly to 6803 and AY port bits instead of copying MAME's handler logic.

findings.note: Tiles are fetched from a 9-bit hcnt/vcnt (0x080-0x1FF horizontally) rather than drawn as a tilemap per frame. Attribute and code bytes are latched on hcnt_scrolled phases 000/100, the graphics-ROM address is formed on phase 111, and the pixel bits are serialized per pixel.

The char RAM address mux hands the bus to the CPU only on pixel phases the video fetch does not use. CPU writes and readback are gated by hcnt_scrolled_flip(1 downto 0) /= "00", the way shared board RAM is arbitrated. MAME's videoram_w is a plain write plus a dirty mark.

findings.signal: sprite RAM scanned by counter bits
findings.note: A free-running spr_hcnt addresses sprite RAM through bit slices (9..4 & 1..0), and the Y/attribute/code/X bytes are latched on fixed counter phases. MAME instead loops over spriteram offsets in a C for-loop.

findings.signal: vertical hit by adder and top-bit compare
findings.note: Sprite presence is vcnt_flip + posv - 1 with its top three bits tested for 111, and the low bits feed the ROM row address XORed with the flip bit. This is adder/comparator hardware, unlike MAME's screen-coordinate expression.

Two 256x4 buffers swap on vcnt(0). A pixel is written only while its location still reads 0000, and the output buffer is cleared as it is read. Sprites are scanned in ascending order with first-write-wins, which gives the same priority as MAME's reverse painter loop by a different, hardware-style mechanism.

The two 256x4 char PROMs are concatenated into an RRGGGBBB byte that drives the outputs directly. The sprite path goes line buffer -> inverted address -> 32x8 RGB PROM, and the mix is a simple 'sprite non-zero wins' mux. There is no indirect pen table like MAME's palette init.

A dedicated register snoops writes to 0x9040 and applies them to lines 64-127 (vcnt_flip(7..6)="01"). Other lines use a signed 16-bit value built from scrollram lo/hi, with positive and negative overflow clamped. This is the same rule as MAME's scrollram[0x40] loop and its (x+scrolly) > max_x clamp post-pass, rather than a board-derived counter scheme.

findings.signal: ad hoc sprite enable window and IRQ line
findings.note: The sprite enable band (vcnt ranges per flip) and the IRQ fire points (vcnt 230/448) are empirical constants with no visible derivation from either the board's counters or MAME.

findings.signal: memory map and ROM bank composition
findings.note: The address decode (8000/9000/9100/C820/D000-D004/E000) and the sprite code/bank bits (attr bit 5, code bit 7) match MAME, as any correct core must.

Address decode is partial (mirrored via cpu_addr(14 downto 11)), the AY BDIR/BC1/A9 pins come straight from 6803 port-2 bits, and the MSM5205 reset/sel lines come from AY1 port B. MAME instead edge-detects port-2 writes and calls address_w/data_w.
